retrieval.reason: Retrieved: JPL SSD planetary/satellite physical parameters, JPL approximate planet elements, JPL SBDB API, NASA NSSDC fact sheets, NASA SLS page, NASA Apollo 11 press kit and three NTRS electric-propulsion documents, ULA Atlas V/Vulcan pages and the ESA Vega-C page (see metadata/sources.json). Not retrievable or not stating the numbers: SpaceX pages (JavaScript-rendered), api.spacexdata.com (HTTP 522), Rocket Lab, Aerojet Rocketdyne (403), Blue Origin (429), Arianespace manual; those records remain unverified.

statement: 32 records are verified (25 celestial bodies at core level; engines and stages whose core numeric fields were all checked) against retrieved JPL, NASA (NTRS, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit), ULA and ESA pages. 198 celestial and 44 launch/engine field checks matched; 16 celestial and 13 launch/engine recalled values were wrong or outdated and were replaced by the sourced value. Launch vehicles are verified field by field only (see verified_field_count); everything not checked (e.g. Falcon, Starship, Electron, Ariane, most engines, spacecraft components, instruments, missions) is still unverified, as are two user-supplied tables. Derived values inherit the status of their inputs. Optimization catalog values are estimated/fictional.

known_conflicts.note: User-supplied file ends at flight 56 (2018-06-04); 57 rows. Reliability (56/57) and landing statistics describe the 2010-2018 development era only and must not be extrapolated to Block 5. Origin/license of the Kaggle-derived file is unverified.

86 rows lack a status, 1 status is the truncated value 'Under' (assumed Under Rehabilitation), 340 lack URLs, and 256 of 485 fall into the 'other' category of the keyword classifier (category is derived, unreviewed).
Launch-site strings differ across rows; treated as the same pad (assumption).
Recorded GM (9.62e-5 km3/s2) and mass (1.4762e15 kg) disagree by ~2.4% via GM=G*M; both retained, GM preferred for orbital use; resolve against JPL SSD sat_phys_par.
For irregular bodies (Phobos, Deimos, Bennu, Enceladus) g=mu/R^2 is a spherical approximation; recorded g is a mean/typical value and is not verified.

known_conflicts.preferred: 33.4 MN design value recorded; flight values vary by mission

known_conflicts.note: Recorded liftoff mass minus recorded stage masses leaves ~31 t, more than payload+fairing implies; at least one input (stage dry mass or liftoff mass) is likely off. See analysis/mass_analysis.json.

Recorded stage dry+propellant masses sum exactly to liftoff mass, leaving no room for payload/fairing; ideal dv in propulsion_analysis (~11.6-12 km/s) is therefore an overestimate and not a credible ascent number. Needs retrieval of the payload user's guide.
Core-stage-only accounting (boosters excluded); stack residual is dominated by booster/upper-stage mass, so the ideal-dv total is not a vehicle capability.
Several missions flew Atlas V 401/411/541 variants not in the launch dataset; launch_vehicle_id is null for them.
